To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
radiation induced dark current is caused by interface states in the photodiode and by trapped charge in the thick gate oxide.

total dose induced dark current is mainly due to interface states in the photodiode, and that interface state density measurements provide a good estimate of the total dose induced dark currents in CMOS image sensor.
radiation induced interface state density increases with dose in a linear manner and that the radiation induced dark current is due to interface state generation current.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the radiation induced dark current in the CMOS photodiodes and its correlation with interface state and trapped charge densities.
the development of a CMOS image sensor for space applications, and with the understanding of the mechanisms responsible for radiation induced dark current.
the study of radiation effects on MOS devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the radiation induced dark current in photodiodes is due to an increase of interface state density and a decrease of oxide trapped charge density, and both effects contribute to the radiation-induced dark current.
radiation induced interface states and trapped charge are both responsible for dark current increase in CMOS image sensor.

the dark current is mainly generated by the increase of interface state density and that a significant part of the trapped charges remains in the oxide even after 300°C anneal, leading to an increase of the dark current.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the total ionizing dose dark current in CMOs image sensor is mainly generated by the interface states and the trapped charge density is not a good indicator of dark current.
interface state density and the corresponding generation current is the major contributor to the dark current in CMOIS.
radiation-induced dark current in CMOIS is mainly generated by the interface state SRH mechanism, and that the trapped charge density in STI is much lower than in gate oxide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
radiation induced interface states and trapped charge are the origin of total ionising dose induced dark current.
interface state and trapped charge measurements are complementary techniques for the understanding of total dose induced dark current.
the interface state SRH current is a major contributor to the dark current in the photodiode and the thick-oxide-FETS.
